claim_type_rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined by closed canonical office-holder list: Wikipedia's `Chief Justice of the United States` master article enumerates the 17 men who have served as Chief Justice of the United States Supreme Court (1789-present), with the 17th (John Roberts) being the current incumbent. Filtering to completed-tenure only yields the closed 16-entry universe (John Jay through William Rehnquist) — benchmark window scope clause mirrors `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms`. Universe membership = 'US Chief Justice with completed tenure per Wikipedia Chief Justice of the United States article' — no curator judgment. Per-row cell values (Tenure Start Year + Tenure End Year + Appointing President) are taken from the master article's consolidated office-holders table per cycle-1 audit's source_count=1 confirmation; Earl Warren's start year corrected to 1954 (oath-of-office date, NOT 1953 Senate confirmation) per cycle-1 audit's required staging edit #2. Mirror precedents for closed-canonical office-holder source_defined: `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` (13 NATO Secretaries-General with completed terms — Rutte excluded as incumbent); `booker_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024` + `pulitzer_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024` (closed annual-prize universes).

Era-distribution context (informational, not staged partition column): Founding era 3 (Jay 1789 + Rutledge 1795 + Ellsworth 1796 — all 3 appointed by Washington); Marshall Court 1 (Marshall 1801-1835 — longest tenure 34 years); Antebellum 2 (Taney 1836-1864 + Chase 1864-1873); Gilded Age 3 (Waite 1874-1888 + Fuller 1888-1910 + White 1910-1921); Progressive 2 (Taft 1921-1930 + Hughes 1930-1941); WWII-Korean War 2 (Stone 1941-1946 + Vinson 1946-1953); Civil Rights era 1 (Warren 1954-1969); Conservative era 2 (Burger 1969-1986 + Rehnquist 1986-2005). Single PK Chief Justice.

source_coverage_notes.source_grounding_summary: 1 registered source (Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States: roles = [universe, value]). 16 per-Chief-Justice Wikipedia articles consulted in validation role during curation; they live in validation_cross_checks above (provenance prose), NOT in source_urls, per the artifact contract.

decision_log.decision: claim_type = source_defined (closed-canonical office-holder list with completed-tenure benchmark window)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'The design is sound: 16 completed-tenure Chief Justices, Roberts excluded as incumbent, temporal primary, set_filter secondary, claim_type=source_defined, Law/Judiciary, and people/judges all work.' US Chief Justice is a constitutional office with a closed canonical sequence (1789-present, 17 office-holders). Filtering to completed-tenure status yields 16 entries (Roberts excluded as incumbent). Mirror precedent: NATO Secretary-General (13 numbered + completed terms, Rutte excluded as incumbent). No curator judgment for universe membership; deterministic universe rule.

decision_log.decision: Benchmark window = completed-tenure Chief Justices only (16 rows); Roberts excluded as incumbent
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'using the first 16 completed tenures is the same defensible pattern as the NATO SG incumbent exclusion.' Roberts took oath September 29, 2005 and is still serving as of 2026-05-18; his End Year is open. Excluding him keeps the staged universe locked to closed tenures with stable Start/End Year values. When Roberts eventually retires/dies, universe extends from 16 → 17 (or more if multiple successors in benchmark window) — temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this.

decision_log.decision: source_count = 1 (master only, NOT 17 as cycle-1 design proposed) — cycle-1 audit's required staging edit #1
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit: 'The master Chief Justice of the United States article supplies all four staged cells: name, tenure dates, and appointer. Per-justice articles can be validation prose, but they should not be registered as value-role sources unless staging adds cells not present in the master.' Master supplies all 4 cells uniformly via its consolidated office-holders table. Per-Justice articles redundantly carry tenure values but are validation cross-checks in provenance prose, NOT registered URLs per artifact-contract canonical vocab. Mirror precedents: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` source_count=1; `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` source_count=1; `global_200_tropical_moist_broadleaf_forest_ecoregions_by_realm` source_count=1.

decision_log.decision: Earl Warren Tenure Start Year = 1954 (NOT 1953) — cycle-1 audit's required staging edit #2
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit: 'The master table notes that the start date is the date the chief justice took the oath of office. Warren was confirmed in 1953 but his listed tenure start is March 1, 1954, so the staged Tenure Start Year should be 1954 if the column is truly tenure start year.' Cycle-1 preview committed 1953 (Senate confirmation date); corrected to 1954 (oath-of-office date) per master convention. The oath-of-office date convention is the locked rule for all 16 staged Tenure Start Year cells.

decision_log.decision: Schema = 4 cols (Chief Justice PK + Tenure Start Year + Tenure End Year + Appointing President); NO 5th cell
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: '4 columns are sufficient; no fifth column needed.' Master article supplies all 4 cells uniformly via consolidated office-holders table. Additional cells (Tenure Length Years / Birth State / Notable Decisions) would require curator computation or per-Justice extraction, defeating source_count=1. Mirror precedent: `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` 4-col schema (Secretary-General + Term Start + Term End + Birth Country).

decision_log.decision: Tenure Start Year convention = oath-of-office date (NOT Senate-confirmation date)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit's required staging edit #2 + master article convention. The master table's 'Start of tenure' column shows the oath-of-office date for each Chief Justice. Examples: Warren confirmed October 5, 1953 / oath March 1, 1954 → Start Year = 1954; Rehnquist confirmed September 17, 1986 / oath September 26, 1986 → Start Year = 1986 (same year for both confirmation and oath). Lock to oath-of-office year per master.

decision_log.decision: Tenure End Year convention = year tenure ended (death or retirement)
decision_log.rationale: Per master article: End Year is the year the Chief Justice's tenure ended via death, retirement, or other cause. Examples: Marshall died July 6, 1835 → End Year = 1835; Rehnquist died September 3, 2005 → End Year = 2005; Vinson died September 8, 1953 → End Year = 1953. Lock to master's stated End Year per office-holders table.

decision_log.decision: John Rutledge IS in universe (recess-appointed Chief Justice rejected by Senate)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'John Rutledge belongs in the universe: the master list includes him as the second Chief Justice and notes he was the only recess-appointed justice not subsequently confirmed by the Senate.' Rutledge was appointed by Washington as recess Chief Justice in August 1795, served until Senate rejection December 15, 1795. Tenure Start Year = 1795; Tenure End Year = 1795. Counted as the 2nd Chief Justice per master canonical numbering.

decision_log.decision: Edward Douglass White Tenure Start Year = 1910 (Chief Justice oath), NOT his earlier Associate Justice tenure
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'Edward Douglass White starts as Chief Justice in 1910, not from his earlier associate-justice tenure; the master note also explains elevated associate justices are separate chief-justice appointments.' White served as Associate Justice 1894-1910, then was elevated to Chief Justice by President Taft in 1910 (oath December 19, 1910). Tenure Start Year cell = 1910 (Chief Justice oath year only).

decision_log.decision: Senate-rejected nominees (not confirmed and not served as Chief Justice) NOT in universe
decision_log.rationale: George H. Williams (Grant 1873, withdrawn before vote) and Caleb Cushing (Grant 1874, withdrawn) were nominated but never confirmed/served. They are NOT in the staged universe (universe requires confirmed-and-served status). Note: Rutledge IS in universe because he was recess-appointed and DID serve briefly before Senate rejection — see Rutledge decision above.

decision_log.decision: Category = temporal primary; secondary = set_filter; operation_type = filter
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'operation_type=filter, query_category=temporal, and secondary_category=set_filter are appropriate.' Temporal primary because the row universe is ordered along the calendar-year axis with Tenure Start Year as the canonical ordering attribute — mirror precedent: `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` (year-keyed); `nber_dated_us_recessions_since_1929` (Peak Year keyed). Secondary set_filter because the universe is set-filtered to completed-tenure membership (Roberts excluded). Operation_type filter mirrors `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` (set-filter by completed-term status).

decision_log.decision: Entity class = people/judges (NEW fine-class extending people bucket from 16 → 17)
decision_log.rationale: Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'people/judges' is the right fine-class. NEW fine-class within the existing people bucket (joining politicians, scientists, athletes, painters, philosophers, laureates, deities, honorees, astronauts, diplomats, authors×2, monarchs, mountaineers, founders). Chief Justices are people in a judicial role — people bucket matches the individual-person framing. Alternative `people/jurists` was considered but `people/judges` is the more common entity-class fine-class naming convention.

Per cycle-1 audit confirmation: 'Law/Judiciary' is correct. Law family currently at 1 instance only (`us_supreme_court_landmark_cases_by_constitutional_amendment` — events/judicial-decisions); this brings Law to 2 with continued judiciary-subdomain focus. Crisis-light Law/Judiciary family chip 1 → 2 — one of 4 (now 3 after Environment chipped this session) families at exactly 1 instance (Health, Law, Food remaining).

normalization_decisions.rule: Name verbatim per Wikipedia per-Chief-Justice article canonical title (which matches master's office-holders table row labels). 16 closed values: John Jay / John Rutledge / Oliver Ellsworth / John Marshall / Roger B. Taney / Salmon P. Chase / Morrison Waite / Melville Fuller / Edward Douglass White / William Howard Taft / Charles Evans Hughes / Harlan F. Stone / Fred M. Vinson / Earl Warren / Warren E. Burger / William Rehnquist. Middle initials preserved where canonical ('Roger B. Taney', 'Salmon P. Chase', 'Harlan F. Stone', 'Fred M. Vinson', 'Warren E. Burger'). Full middle name 'Edward Douglass White' (NOT 'Edward D. White' or 'Edward White'). 'Morrison Waite' (NOT 'Morrison R. Waite' which is also documented in Wikipedia but article title is 'Morrison Waite'). 'Melville Fuller' (NOT 'Melville W. Fuller'). 'William Rehnquist' (NOT 'William H. Rehnquist' which is also documented but article title omits middle initial). Names follow Wikipedia article canonical title — NOT historical newspaper or formal-court conventions.

Integer year of oath of office per master article's 'Start of tenure' column. Convention: Senate-confirmation year is NOT used (Earl Warren confirmed October 5, 1953 → 1953 is INCORRECT; his oath was March 1, 1954 → 1954 is CORRECT). All 16 staged values follow oath-of-office date convention per cycle-1 audit's required staging edit #2. Examples: John Jay oath October 19, 1789 → 1789; John Marshall oath February 4, 1801 → 1801; Roger B. Taney oath March 28, 1836 → 1836; John Rutledge recess-appointment commission August 12, 1795 → 1795 (recess-appointed; sworn briefly before Senate rejection).

Integer year tenure ended via death, retirement, resignation, or Senate rejection per master article's 'End of tenure' column. Examples: John Jay resigned June 29, 1795 → 1795; John Marshall died July 6, 1835 → 1835; John Rutledge Senate rejection December 15, 1795 → 1795 (same year as Start for the recess-appointed-rejected case); Earl Warren retired June 23, 1969 → 1969; William Rehnquist died September 3, 2005 → 2005. May equal Tenure Start Year for short tenures (Rutledge 1795 = Start = End).

Name of the US President who appointed the Chief Justice per master article's office-holders table 'Appointed by' column. Examples: John Jay appointed by George Washington → 'George Washington'; John Marshall appointed by John Adams (Adams' last-month appointment) → 'John Adams'; Roger B. Taney appointed by Andrew Jackson → 'Andrew Jackson'. Note edge cases: (a) Edward Douglass White was elevated from Associate Justice to Chief Justice by President William Howard Taft (1910); Appointing President = 'William Howard Taft' (NOT Cleveland who appointed White as Associate Justice 1894). (b) William Howard Taft himself was later appointed Chief Justice (1921) by President Warren G. Harding (after Taft's own presidency 1909-1913); Appointing President = 'Warren G. Harding'. Lock to master's 'Appointed by' column for each row.

open_questions.question: When John Roberts' tenure eventually ends, should the instance be re-staged to include him?
open_questions.answer: Yes, when Roberts retires/dies, the universe extends from 16 → 17 (or more if multiple successors occur in the benchmark window). Universe is locked to completed-tenure Chief Justices as of 2026-05-18 staging. temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects this — Roberts is the active incumbent (took oath September 29, 2005); future Chief Justice transitions are infrequent (median tenure ~14 years in modern era).

open_questions.question: Should the schema include Tenure Length (Years) as a 5th cell?
open_questions.answer: No — Tenure Length = End Year − Start Year is mathematically derivable from the staged Start/End cells. Per cycle-1 audit: '4 columns are sufficient; no fifth column needed.' Schema kept at 4 cols matching the NATO SG precedent.

open_questions.question: Should Senate-rejected Chief Justice nominees (Williams 1873, Cushing 1874) be in scope?
open_questions.answer: No — universe requires confirmed-and-served status. Williams and Cushing were nominated but withdrawn before Senate vote (never confirmed, never served). The ONLY Senate-rejected nominee in the universe is John Rutledge — he was a recess-appointed Chief Justice who DID serve briefly (August-December 1795) before Senate rejection; counted as the 2nd Chief Justice per master canonical numbering.

open_questions.question: Why excludes incumbent Roberts instead of including him with End Year = current year?
open_questions.answer: Mirror precedent `nato_secretaries_general_birth_country_terms` excluded incumbent Rutte under the same rationale: completed-tenure benchmark scope. Including an active incumbent with End Year = 2026 (current year) would create an unstable cell value that changes annually until tenure ends. Excluding incumbent locks the universe to historically-closed tenures with stable Start/End Year values. When Roberts' tenure ends, the universe naturally extends.

open_questions.question: How are middle-initial conventions handled for Chief Justices with multiple naming styles?
open_questions.answer: Per the Wikipedia per-Chief-Justice article canonical title. Examples: 'Roger B. Taney' (article title uses middle initial 'B'); 'Edward Douglass White' (article title uses full middle name 'Douglass' NOT 'Edward D. White'); 'Morrison Waite' (article title omits middle initial 'R' that appears in some historical sources); 'William Rehnquist' (article title omits middle initial 'H' that appears in some sources). NO curator override of master/article-title conventions.
